[[File:Greyling 0S.png|thumb|A [[greyling]], an aggressive creature found in the [[Meadows]].]] '''Creatures''' are non-player characters which are found throughout ''[[Valheim (world)|Valheim]]''. They can be split to four categories: * [[Creatures#Bosses|Bosses]] are powerful aggressive creatures that must be summoned. Killing them unlocks [[Forsaken power|Forsaken powers]], increases [[Global Keys|world difficulty]] and provides loot to progress in the game. * [[Creatures#Minibosses|Minibosses]] are unique, named, aggressive creatures that you can find in specific dungeons. Killing any given miniboss will reward with one of [[Hildir's Chests]]. * [[Creatures#Aggressive creatures|Aggressive creatures]] will attack players when alerted. They also drop loot when killed. * [[Creatures#Passive creatures|Passive creatures]] provide resources when killed (or harvested). They will never attack players. * [[Creatures#NPCs|NPCs]] are friendly creatures/characters that cannot be killed and may provide some service or help to the player. == Bosses == Bosses, also known as the '''Forsaken''', can be summoned by offering specific items (hinted by the [[Runestone#Altar Runestones|Runestones]]) at their specific spawn site. They have increased HP and special attacks compared to regular creatures. A boss site is automatically marked on the player's map by reading the runestone in the specific biomes. There are multiple spawn locations for every boss. One-star creatures have double the health and deal 150% damage, while two-stars have triple the health and deal double damage. '''Behavior''' *Creatures will give up chasing after unable to attack for 60 seconds or unable to detect the target for 30 seconds. *Some creatures have a max chase range. After chasing that far they will give up if unable to detect the target for 1 seconds. *After unable to attack for 15 seconds, creatures will focus structures for 15 seconds if they can't reach the target. *Creatures only attack walls and doors if they aren't able to reach the target player. *Some creatures are afraid of fire and will flee from it. *Some creatures try to avoid fire and will be passive near it. *Some creatures circulate around the target while waiting to attack. *Swimming creatures try to flee towards water if forced on ground. *Creatures passively regenerate 1.67% of their max health every minute (100% over 60 minutes). *Creatures gain +30% more effective health per each additional player within 100 meters. E.g. 3 players = +60% effective health. **This is updated whenever the creature takes damage. *Creatures gain +4% more damage per each additional player within 100 meters. See the taming and breeding sections below. == Drops == {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Boar trophy|0star=15%|1star=15%|2star=15%}} {{drop row|item=Leather scraps|0star=1|1star=2|2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Boar meat|0star=1|1star=2|2star=4}}}} == Spawning == {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Anywhere]] in [[Meadows]]|limit=4|stars=After 800 meters from the world center}} {{spawn row|type=1-9 [[spawn points]] near [[Runestone|Boar runestones]]|frequency=0}} {{spawn row|type=0-2 [[spawn points]] near abandoned farms in [[Meadows]]|frequency=0}} {{spawn row|type=From breeding|limit=5, within 10 meters|frequency=-|stars=Inherited from either parent, randomly}} {{spawn row|type=During "Eikthyr rallies the creatures of the forest," [[Events|event]] before defeating [[Eikthyr]]|limit=2|frequency=6|stars=No}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones]] in [[Meadows#Alternative biomes|Peaceful Meadows]]|limit=15|frequency=5|stars=Yes}} }} == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating boars|Aggressive creature strategies#Boar}} === Attack === Swings its head upward and hits in a 45.2-degree horizontal arc with a range of 1.5 meters (10 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] damage). This attack can be used every 5 seconds when within 2 meters of a player. == Taming == ''For general taming information and strategies, see [[Taming]].'' To tame a wild Boar, players should approach while sneaking to avoid alarming it. If a Boar feels threatened, it will become aggressive, chasing the player until they are out of sight, at which point it will revert to a 'hungry' state. Wild Boars have a predictable combat pattern, charging and then retreating, which can be used to the player's advantage when herding them into a pen ''(recommended to tame)''. Constructing a secure pen is essential to prevent the Boar from escaping and to avoid disruption of the taming process by outside sources. To successfully tame a Boar, players need to feed it {{item link|Raspberries}}, {{item link|Blueberries}}, {{item link|Carrot}}s, {{item link|Onion}}s, {{item link|Turnip}}s, or red {{item link|Mushroom}}s. They will ignore all other foods dropped on the ground. Just drop the food on the ground within one meter, and the Boar will eat, as long as it is not frightened ''(indicated by a red exclamation mark)''. Players can place the food on the ground in a stack, as the Boar will only eat one food from the stack at a time. The taming speed is 30 minutes of real-life gameplay with three pieces of food, '''uninterrupted'''; as long as the Boar does not get frightened and the correct amount of food is on the ground, it should only take 30 minutes. A player must remain in the area for taming to progress. If the Boar becomes frightened at any time during taming, the process will take longer and may require more food. == Tamed == When tamed, Boars seek freedom. If a tamed Boar sees an opening in their fenced area, they will run towards it, which can be used to corral them from place to place. Tamed Boars can be renamed by pressing LShift + E. Interacting with them using E will display the message "(Creature name) loves you" on-screen along with a cloud of pink hearts. They are no longer afraid of fire and require feeding for passive health regeneration. Additionally, tamed Boars lose their anchor to their spawn point, allowing them to move more freely. '''Note:''' ''Boars from abandoned farms and Runestones will retain their anchor point and will always try to return home, making them more challenging to handle. It is recommended to either breed these boars on the spot and move the offspring instead, or to name the original tamed animal and then, once bred, kill it. One issue with using the original animal is that it tends to sit in a corner of a pen, staring at its spawn point, which can interfere with breeding as it does not roam the pen.'' == Breeding == Tamed Boars can breed, provided the Boar is happy and well-fed with berries, carrots, onions, turnips or red mushrooms, along with there being another Boar at least within three meters, and no more than five Boars within at least 10 meters. Once the conditions are met, the Boar will accumulate love points (3) with one another until the pregnancy starts. Successful love point is indicated by pink hearts. After gaining enough love points, the Boar becomes pregnant, which is not visualized. After one minute, the Boar gives birth to a baby Boar ''(piglet)'', visualized by a red cloud. Any Boar can become pregnant, which means that if two Boars breed and one becomes pregnant, they still have the ability to breed and get the other pregnant. Once born, the '''piglet''' will take 50 minutes to mature into an adult. Offspring inherit [[Creature Level|stars]] from the parent that gives birth to it. Offspring are tamed at birth and require a [[Butcher Knife]] or friendly fire to kill. Offspring cannot be interacted with ''(no renaming or commanding)'' until they become an adult. {| class="wikitable" |Creature |Required love points |Total limit |Partner check range |Pregnancy duration |Birth offset |Offspring grow time |Offspring drops |- |[[Boar]] |3 |5 within 10 meters |3 meters |1 minute |1 meter |50 minutes |None |} == Gallery == Boar2.jpg Boar lore.jpg Boar 1star in-game.png Boar 2star in-game.png == Notes == * Boars will not eat [[Yellow Mushroom]]s. {{Creatures}} [[Category:Aggressive creatures]] [[ru:Кабан]] [[fr:Sanglier]] [[cs:Kanec]] [[uk:Вепр]] [[de:Wildschwein]] [[pt-br:Javali]]

'''Bonemass''' is the third [[Creatures#Bosses|boss]]. He appears as a gigantic humanoid mass comprised of toxic ooze, mud and skeletal remains, likely absorbed from nearby tombs situated close to his altar.

== Summoning ==
[[File:BonemassAltar.png|left|thumb|200x200px|Bonemass' Forsaken Altar.]]
Bonemass' [[Forsaken Altars|Forsaken Altar]] is located in [[Swamp]]s. His location can be found when visiting [[Sunken Crypts]] and sometimes ruined structures, where a [[Runestone#Vegvisir|Vegvisir]] will reveal his nearest summoning location on the map.

He is summoned by placing 10 {{Item Link|Withered Bone}}s in his Forsaken altar in Swamps. Like all bosses, Bonemass can be summoned as many times as desired, provided the required materials are met.

== Attacks and abilities ==
{{For|strategies for defeating Bonemass|Boss strategies#Bonemass}}
Bonemass has an environment aura that forces raining, which means pulling him from the area cannot be used to remove [[Wet Effect|Wet]].

=== Area of effect ===
Bonemass will charge up with a thick green cloud before vomiting a wave of poisonous ooze, inflicting the [[Poison]] status on everything in a 9-meter radius around him (130 [[Damage types#Poison|Poison]] damage). This is signaled when he leans backwards. The poison cloud persists for 15 seconds and will continuously refresh the poison duration on any player that stays inside. This effect cannot be dodged or blocked. Bonemass can use this ability when a player is within 15 meters, and it has a cooldown of 30 seconds. The cloud is centered on the impact point of Bonemass's vomit; due to the size of his collision box, this results in the cloud not reaching very far behind him which gives players a safe area to retreat to that is still within range to strike him.

=== Punch ===
A close-range swipe at a player dealing up to 80 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] and 50 [[Damage types#Poison|Poison]] damage to players, in addition to 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage to any trees or rocks hit. This attack can be used every 7 seconds when a player is within 8 meters. It hits in a horizontal 8.5-meter 66.1-degree arc in front of Bonemass.

=== Throw ===
At 50-second intervals, Bonemass will reach into his armpit to throw out a glob of goop in the general direction of the player at an initial velocity of 20 meters per second with a spread of 5–20 degrees. On impact, this ability will attempt to spawn four random monsters ([[Skeleton]]s and/or [[Blob]]s, with equal chances for both). A maximum of eight summons of each type can be active at once; but the selection of enemies each spawning instance is still random regardless of the status of spawn caps, meaning reaching the spawn cap for one type of summon will not force spawns for the other. Bonemass will still attempt to summon creatures even if both spawn caps are reached. This ability can only be used when a player is within 30 meters.

== Aftermath ==
Defeating Bonemass provides the player with a Wishbone, which allows the player to easily locate [[Silver Vein]]s beneath the surface of [[Mountain]] biomes (as well as buried [[Muddy Scrap Pile]]s in Swamp biomes, and other miscellaneous buried treasures in certain locations).

=== Forsaken power ===
Mounting Bonemass' trophy upon his respective stone will allow the player to claim his Forsaken Power. This ability will grant the player and nearby allies the following effects for 300 seconds:

* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Blunt
* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Slash
* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Pierce
* Block stamina usage: -100%
* Block stamina return: +5

See [[Forsaken_power#Bonemass Power|Bonemass' power]] for more details.

=== Events ===
Defeating Bonemass affects the following [[events]] for that world:

* Disables: Draugr and Skeleton "A foul smell from the swamp..."
* Enables: Blobs and Oozers "A foul smell from the swamp..."
* Enables: "A skeleton surprise!"
* Enables: "A cold wind blows from the mountains." (if [[Moder]] has not been defeated)
* Enables: "There's a smell of sulfur in the air." (if a [[Surtling]] has died)
* Enables: "You are being hunted."
* Enables: "You stirred the cauldron." (if a [[Bat]] has died)
* Enables: "You feel a chill down your spine..."
Note: Two of these events unlock flying enemies that will be uninhibited by base walls and will attack tame animals. For example, bats will quickly wipe out any outdoor tame Boars (if the player has them), most likely before the player can swat them all. Therefore, in order to protect any rare animals (such as a 2-star [[Boar]]), it is advisable to build a secure indoor barn area before undertaking Bonemass.

Defeating Bonemass unlocks [[Skeleton]]s to spawn at night in the Meadows, Black Forest, Swamp (additional), Mountain and Plains. They can only have 0 stars.

'''Creature level''' determines the damage, health and the amount of dropped items by [[creatures]].

== Description ==
A creature's level is indicated by the number of stars displayed next to the creature's name.

* Level 1 – 0 stars
* Level 2 – 1 star  (⭐)
* Level 3 – 2 stars (⭐⭐)

In addition to the stars, there will also be some visual differences between the levels. Depending on the creature, they may have more features, a different color or a bigger size.

==Effects==

*+50% damage per level
* +100% health per level
* 2x drops per level (excluding [[Trophies]])
* 2x drop chance per level (up to 100%, excluding [[Trophies]])

For example [[Greydwarf]] health is 40/80/120 and damage from stone throw attack is 10/15/20 depending on the level. [[Greydwarf Eye]] is dropped 1/2/4 per level with a 50%/100%/100% chance.

Creature damage is further increased by 4% and effective health is further increased by 30% for each additional player within 100 meters. These are also applied to tamed creatures. This scaling caps at 5 players.

Internally the effective health increase from additional players is implemented as a damage reduction so that it can be scaled dynamically. The reduction doesn't apply to shown damage number so it's not visible to the players. For practical purposes, it can be considered as a health increase.

== Leveling ==
Creatures have a random chance to level up when they are spawned. The random chance is 0%, 10% or 15% per level depending on the source of spawning, the creature being spawned and in some cases the distance from the world center. The random chance is not affected by world progression or the amount of days.

Following rules determine the random chance:

* 0% chance for bosses ([[Eikthyr]], [[The Elder]], [[Bonemass]], [[Moder]], [[Yagluth]], [[The Queen]] and [[Fader]]).
* 0% chance for [[Events|event]] creatures.
* 0% chance for following creatures: [[Abomination]], [[Blob]], [[Deathsquito]], [[Drake]], [[Fenring]], [[Fuling Shaman]], [[Ghost]], [[Greyling]], [[Lox]], [[Oozer]], [[Root (creature)|Root]], [[Serpent]], [[Stone Golem]], [[Wraith]], [[Seeker Brood]], [[Fallen Valkyrie]], [[Bonemaw]] and [[Volture]].
* 10% chance for [[spawn points]] (mostly one time), excluding [[Draugr]] and creatures listed above.
* 15% chance for [[Creature spawner|creature spawners]].
* 0% chance for [[spawn zones]] within 800 meters of the world center: [[Boar]], [[Neck]].
* 0% chance for [[spawn zones]] within 2000 meters of the world center: [[Greydwarf Brute]] (Black forest), [[Troll]].
* 0% or 10% chance for other [[spawn zones]] (see the page for more information).
* 100% chance when breeding based on the parent (about 50% chance when breeding creatures with different levels).

Each level up is rolled one by one. For example [[Deer]] have a 10% chance roll to reach level 2 (⭐) and then if successful, another 10% chance to reach level 3 (⭐⭐). Therefore 1% of all Deer will be level 3 (⭐⭐) (10%*10%) and 9% of all Deer will be level 2 (⭐) (10%-1%).

Needed to craft a [[Fishing Hat]]

==Notes==
* Has a unique line: "Do you ever wonder what lurks in the deepest parts of the ocean? Don't. It's better not to know."

He appears as a charred, skeletal dragon which emanates a green glow from orifices and gaps in his body. == Summoning == The Emerald Flame's summoning altar can be found in a coliseum-like structure in the Ashlands. The [[Runestone|Vegvisir]] can be found in the central tower of [[Charred Fortress]]es and very rarely on top of [[Charred Ruins]], revealing the nearest summoning altar on the map. Under 35% health, it can be used every 20 seconds. The flames last for 15 seconds and cannot be dodged nor blocked. Fader can use this attack when he's within 40 meters of a player. === Bite === Fader pulls his head back and then lunges forward to bite in a 10-meter 40-degree horizontal arc in front of him (210 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]], 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack can be used every 3 seconds when within 9 meters of a player. === Claw === Fader brings up one of his paws and swipes in an area in a 10-meter 65-degree horizontal arc in front of him (200 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]], 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack has two variants, each with its own 3-second cooldown: a slash with his left claw and a slash with his right claw. He can use this attack when within 9 meters of a player. === Spin === Fader leans slightly on his right side before spinning to attack the surrounding area in a 8.5-meter radius circle around himself (140 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]], 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 300 Tier 3 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). He can use this ability every 20 seconds when a player is within 8 meters. === Flamebreath === Fader charges up and releases a 17-meter line of fire. It leaves lingering fire on the ground with a radius of 4 meters that inflicts the [[Burning]] status (60 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]], 40 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). The flames last for 14 seconds. This attack cannot be blocked and can only be used every 25 seconds between 5–85% health when within 2–20 meters of a player. === Meteors === Fader rises on his hind legs and then stomps onto the ground calling forth 10 meteors, similar to [[Yagluth|Yagluth's]] meteor attack (40 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 120 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]], 100 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 100 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). The meteors fall from the sky 60 meters behind Fader and 90 meters off of the ground in a 15-meter radius sphere. Upon impact, they leave green flames in a 5-meter radius circle that inflicts the [[Burning]] status (80 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]], 80 [[Damage types#Spirit|Spirit]], 30 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 30 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damageDue to what is presumably a typo or balancing change, this attack does not actually use the Fader_MeteorSmash_AOE prefab but instead uses the Fader_WallOfFire_AOE prefab. He can use this ability while a player is within 30 meters. === Roar === When a player is within 100 meters, Fader can shoot eight glowing orbs out of his mouth into that air directly above him. These travel at an initial velocity of 20–50 meters per second for up to 20 seconds before despawning. They have a spread of 20–60 degrees. Similar to the [[Wolf]], Level 3 (two-star) Asksvin only spawn at night. Like any creatures spawned at night, Level 3 Asksvin will attempt to flee the active area and despawn during daytime hours if the taming process has not begun. This can be prevented by either (A) trapping them in a pit or pen that they cannot escape (and staying within 64 meters of them) or (B) by starting the taming process, after which they will never despawn. Asksvin can be tamed by feeding them [[Smoke Puff]]s, [[Vineberry Cluster]]s or [[Fiddlehead]]s. They are rideable by equipping the [[Asksvin Saddle]]. When riding an Asksvin, players cannot attack. Players riding an Asksvin can traverse lava, and neither the player nor Asksvin will take damage from the lava. Tamed Asksvin do not do friendly fire damage to players, any other tamed creatures or neutral [[Dvergr (race)|Dvergr]]. == Breeding == Asksvin can breed, provided the Asksvin is happy and well-fed with [[Fiddlehead]] or [[Vineberry Cluster]] or [[Smoke Puff]], along with there being another Asksvin within four meters, and no more than 10 Asksvin within at least 10 meters. Once the conditions are met, they will accumulate love points with one another until the pregnancy starts. Pregnancy lasts 60 seconds, checked every 30 seconds, so the egg comes 60 to 90 seconds after it starts. They then lay an [[Asksvin egg]]. The quality of the Asksvin egg is determined by the Asksvin that laid it. A quality 1 egg in the player's inventory indicates a 0-star Asksvin, quality 2 indicates a 1-star, and quality 3 indicates a 2-star. Once laid, it would take 30 minutes to hatch into Asksvin Hatchling if there is a heat source nearby (Example [[Campfire]]). If the heat source is gone or the player puts the egg into their inventory, the timer is reset. Then the Asksvin Hatchling takes 50 minutes to grow into an adult without the need of heat source. They will not breed if the cap is reached, which is 10 Asksvin in 10 meters. However, there is currently no known limit to the eggs themselves. == Trivia == * The word "Asksvin" is Swedish for "ash swine." And like swine, the plural for Asksvin is the same as its singular form. * Due to their green and warty appearance, "Pickle-Dog" has gained popularity as a common moniker for Asksvin within the Twitch-Valheim community. {{Creatures}} [[uk:Попелозавр]] [[ru:Пеплозавр]]

'''Gammeltrolls''' are huge hostile creatures that roam around the [[Deep North]]. They are elder [[Troll]]s, the largest creatures in all of ''Valheim''.

Gammeltrolls are essential for progression in the Deep North. Upon being defeated, they turn into statues as [[Petrified Gammeltroll]]s. Those become part of the terrain and can be built on, or blown up to obtain [[Petrified Tissue]], the raw source of [[Bloodgold]], the Deep North-tier metal.

Gammeltrolls are resistant to most physical damage types, except for the weak point on their head.

== Drops ==
Gammeltrolls drop no items themselves. When one dies, it leaves behind a [[Petrified Gammeltroll]], which can only be damaged by Tier 6 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage. Each of its segments yields two or three items, each either [[Stone]] (2/3 chance) or [[Petrified Tissue]] (1/3 chance).

== Spawning ==
{{spawn table|
{{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Anywhere]] in [[Deep North]] above altitude 10, during the day and night, alone|limit=1|frequency=|stars=No}}

The spawn system places a Gammeltroll spawn point, which spawns a single Gammeltroll with a wake-up animation once a player comes within 120 meters. The spawn point does not respawn it.

== Attacks and abilities ==
The punch and ground slam attacks also hit [[Factions|allied creatures]]. A perfect block does not stagger a Gammeltroll.

=== Punch ===
Deals 220 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 6 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 6 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage in a 15-meter, 100-degree horizontal arc. There is a left and a right variant with the same damage, each with its own 4-second cooldown. It can be used within 15 meters of a target.

=== Ground slam ===
Stomps with one foot, dealing 200 Blunt, 100 Tier 2 Chop and 40 Tier 2 Pickaxe damage in a 6-meter, 90-degree vertical arc. There is a left and a right variant with the same damage, each with its own 10-second cooldown. It can be used within 10 meters of a target, in any direction. When a stomp hits anything, including the ground, it also creates a 10-meter area that deals 220 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 4 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 100 Tier 4 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage. Unlike the stomp itself, this area does not hit allied creatures.

=== Throw ===
Throws eight projectiles in two bursts of four, 0.2 seconds apart. Each projectile deals 150 Blunt, 100 Chop and 80 Pickaxe damage in a 5-meter radius where it lands, and leaves a half log behind. The logs can be chopped for three items, each either [[Wood]] (2/3 chance) or [[Timberwood]] (1/3 chance). This attack can be used every 12 seconds when 12–300 meters from a target.

== Notes ==
* Their punch attack has enough [[Damage#Terrain damage|tool tier]] to mine a Petrified Gammeltroll.
** This means that, in theory, a player could obtain Deep North tier weapons and armor as early as after [[Moder]].
* Gammeltrolls stand 21 meters (68.9 feet) tall, triple the height of a Black Forest Troll.
